Leolani
A Knowledge-Graph- Driven Chat Agent
Grounding a lifestyle-coaching conversation in a living knowledge graph — architecture, conversational strategies, and a live example.
Piek Vossen — Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
cltl-kg-driven-chat
Type 2 diabetes self-management
Why this agent exists
A coach that remembers, not just a chatbot that replies
Structured diary construction
Every turn is turned into semantic-role triples and pushed into a knowledge graph — a persistent, queryable record of what the person actually did and felt.
The graph drives the dialogue
What's still missing in the graph — not a fixed script — decides the agent's next question, so the conversation stays grounded in this person's own history.
Built for Type 2 diabetes
Diet, exercise, sleep, mood, medication and symptoms — everyday factors that shape blood-sugar management, tracked over time, not just one session.
Building on structured-diary and synthetic-dialogue work for functioning & well-being monitoring — see References.

Incremental, not batch — one LLM call per turn keeps the running history, so "it" and "that" still resolve to the right earlier activity.
One id per real-world event — the same activity_id is reused every time it's mentioned again, even with no new phrase.
Pronouns become identities — "I" and "you" link to a real person's URI, not a bare, unlinked word.
One shared role vocabulary — agent, patient, location, time, qualification — under the project's own n2mu: namespace.

The corpus becomes a memory
An event-centric knowledge graph, not a transcript
Jan says
"I'm concerned about my frequent thirst and dry mouth."
thirst_and_dry_mouth_1

EventSeries

Jan

Every mention is an EventSeries instance — not a flat triple. The same identifier is reused every time thirst comes up again, exactly like activity_id in this agent's own graph.
Perspective travels with the event — attributedTo links it to an attribution node carrying the speaker's emotion, factuality and certainty. A memory, not just a fact.

Conversational strategy — deciding what's missing
Two ways to spot a knowledge gap
kg_gap_finder.py
Peer statistics
Compares an activity to similar past instances. A gap fires once a majority of peers share the missing predicate.
Limit: the very first instance of a kind has no peers yet — no gap can ever fire for it.
intent_gap_finder.py
Hand-authored intents
One JSON file per topic — diet, exercise, sleep, symptoms, medication, conditions, measurements — each stating what a complete record needs.
Works from the very first mention — the expectation is declared, not inferred from peers.
Same per-turn loop either way — KgChatSession vs. KgIntentChatSession swap only the gap-finding step.

Conversational strategy — one intent, in order
Ask one thing at a time, in priority order
1 · What
patient_type
What was eaten, drunk, taken or measured
2 · How much / long
qualification
Duration, degree, quantity — only once step 1 is known
3 · When
activity_date
Any time value at all — only once 1 and 2 are filled
4 · Extra detail
secondary objectives
Only reached once 1–3 are all satisfied
measurement_intents.json, in practice
"Did you measure blood sugar level lately?" → "What did you measure?" (quantity) → "When did you measure it?" — each question only paraphrases the intent's own hand-written template, so a weaker model never leaks a raw role name like "patient" into the question.

Conversational strategy — getting the answer to stick
Capture the answer, don't lose it to a coreference miss
Confirm, don't interrogate
A missing "who" is asked as "Was that you?" — not an open question. Yes / no / a correction is pushed straight to the graph.
Attach the reply directly
A single-predicate gap arms a pending slot. The next reply is classified ANSWER / DECLINE / UNRELATED and written straight onto that same activity — never left for the extractor to re-link.
Never ask forever
Two backstops: a gap already asked is never repeated, and a requirement gets a fixed number of tries across the whole chat before the agent moves on.
Why it matters: a short reply like "30 minutes" often gets coreferenced onto a brand-new, empty subject — direct capture skips that guesswork entirely.

Conversational strategy — never a dead end
An acknowledgement is never the whole reply
Before
"Thanks for letting me know."
The reply, and the conversation, just stop there.
After
"No worries, thanks for letting me know. How has your exercise been going lately?"
Same acknowledgement — immediately chained into the next open topic.
Every acknowledgement now calls straight into the agent's own reply function afterward — the exact call the conversation would make anyway once nothing else is pending, made explicit so it always fires.

Takeaways
Grounded, paced, and never a dead end
The graph — not a script — decides the next question, from the very first mention of a topic.
Sessions open by measuring the real gap against this person's own history, then ask until there's genuinely enough.
Answers are captured directly and never asked for twice; acknowledgements always keep the conversation moving.
Every fact is visible, live, in a graph panel colored and de-duplicated for a human to actually read.

Reconstructing lifestyles from conversations between Diabetes patients and a coach. LREC 2026 (under review) — the conversational corpus and event-centric knowledge graph behind this agent's memory.
